data.name: Occultus - Mediterranean Cabal
data.detailed_description:
Sicília, no começo da década de 1900...

O neto de um renomado comerciante de antiguidades desembarca em Palermo para visitar seu avô. Recém chegado na cidade, ele descobre que seu avô foi raptado e sua loja saqueada.
No chão, ele encontra um recado preocupante a respeito de uma missa que aconteceria naquela mesma noite a zero hora. O rapaz decide seguir essa pista, que o levará a uma procura bastante misteriosa.

Mergulhe em uma investigação incrível que levará você às paisagens mais suntuosas da Itália. Desvende vários cenários em busca de objetos escondidos e resolva quebra-cabeças sempre mais desafiantes. O tempo é curto. Esteja com seus neurônios a postos!

*Cenários extraordinários com objetos escondidos
*Uma grande variedade de mini-jogos e enigmas
*Explore paisagens suntuosas na Itália do início da década de 1900
*Cenários alternados de dia e à noite
*Personagens intrigantes em meio de uma investigação no mundo do ocultismo

reviews.review:
Occultus - Mediterranean Cabal takes the familiar hidden-object adventure formula and gives it an appealing Mediterranean identity built around mystery, historical surroundings, and supernatural intrigue. Developed by Sylphe Labs and published by M.INDIE, the game is primarily aimed at players who enjoy methodical exploration, visual searches, traditional puzzles, and stories involving secret organizations. Rather than relying on action or demanding mechanical systems, it encourages players to investigate carefully and gradually uncover the truth behind a strange disappearance.

The story begins when the protagonist travels to Palermo, Sicily, intending to visit his grandfather, an established antique dealer. What should have been an ordinary reunion quickly becomes unsettling when the grandfather is nowhere to be found and his antique shop has clearly been vandalized. Among the remaining clues is a mysterious note concerning a midnight Mass. Following this lead pulls the protagonist into an increasingly suspicious investigation where apparently ordinary locations conceal connections to something considerably darker. The personal nature of the disappearance provides a simple but effective motivation for continuing deeper into the mystery.

One of the game's better qualities is its choice of setting. Early twentieth-century Italy provides considerably more character than the generic haunted houses and fantasy locations frequently associated with casual hidden-object adventures. Palermo's old buildings, antique-filled rooms, religious imagery, shadowy streets, cemeteries, and underground locations naturally complement the occult themes. The game also makes use of both daytime and nighttime environments, allowing familiar surroundings to develop a different personality once darkness arrives. This helps create an atmosphere that is mysterious and occasionally ominous without turning the experience into outright horror.

Gameplay remains firmly rooted in classic hidden-object design. Players move between illustrated locations, examine their surroundings, locate concealed objects, collect useful items, and determine where those items should be used. Hidden-object sequences are mixed with environmental puzzles and standalone minigames, providing some welcome variation. The mechanics are straightforward enough that newcomers should quickly understand the basic structure, while experienced fans will recognize almost every major convention immediately. This accessibility is useful, although it also means the game rarely surprises players with radically different mechanics.

The hidden-object scenes place considerable importance on observation. Environments can contain many decorative elements, and finding the required objects sometimes demands close examination rather than rapid clicking. The detailed backgrounds work particularly well for this style of gameplay because the locations feel appropriately cluttered without completely losing their visual identity. There can still be occasions when an item feels difficult to spot simply because it blends into the scenery, but that is an inherent part of the genre and may actually appeal to players seeking a more patient visual challenge.

Puzzle variety gives the adventure additional substance. Progress is periodically interrupted by riddles, mechanisms, pattern-based challenges, and other minigames that require more than simply identifying objects on a list. Some solutions are relatively easy to determine, while others encourage experimentation and closer attention to available clues. None of this transforms Occultus into an exceptionally difficult puzzle game, but the changing challenges prevent the investigation from becoming too repetitive. The puzzles also fit reasonably well with the larger theme of deciphering a conspiracy rather than feeling completely disconnected from the adventure.

The narrative is more successful at generating curiosity than developing complicated characters. The missing grandfather, damaged antique shop, strange midnight gathering, and references to a secret cabal create enough questions to keep the investigation moving forward. The story gradually introduces increasingly unusual circumstances, giving players the sense that the initial disappearance is only one part of something much larger. However, anyone expecting a deeply branching detective narrative or extensive character development should temper those expectations. Storytelling mainly provides context and momentum for exploration and puzzle solving.

Visually, the hand-crafted locations remain one of the most appealing elements. There is a pleasant old-fashioned adventure-game quality to the presentation, particularly when moving through historical interiors and atmospheric outdoor environments. The shift between brighter Mediterranean scenery and darker nighttime locations reinforces the contrast between ordinary life and the secretive activities being investigated. The supernatural elements are handled with enough restraint that the game remains approachable for players interested in occult themes without necessarily wanting an intense horror experience.

Pacing is deliberately relaxed. There is little pressure to react quickly, so players can spend time examining backgrounds, considering clues, and working through puzzles. That makes it particularly suitable for casual sessions. The drawback is that players accustomed to modern adventure games featuring extensive animation, cinematic presentation, complex dialogue systems, or unrestricted exploration may consider the experience dated. Its strengths come from traditional point-and-click principles rather than contemporary production spectacle.

Replay value is fairly modest because discovering solutions is a significant part of the appeal. Once the locations, hidden objects, puzzles, and major revelations are familiar, subsequent playthroughs inevitably lose some of their mystery. It is therefore best treated as a focused single-player adventure that provides its strongest experience during the initial journey.

Steam Deck compatibility should be approached with some caution. The game's comparatively simple point-and-click mechanics and modest technical demands make handheld play potentially practical, particularly through trackpad or touchscreen-style interaction. However, without a strong native controller-oriented interface, certain interactions and small visual details may be more comfortable on a larger display with mouse input. It is better regarded as potentially playable through Steam Deck's flexible input options rather than assuming a completely optimized handheld experience.

Overall, Occultus - Mediterranean Cabal is a respectable traditional hidden-object adventure elevated by its unusual Sicilian setting and occult mystery. Its mixture of object hunting, puzzles, atmospheric exploration, and supernatural conspiracy provides a comfortable experience for fans of the genre. It does not radically advance the formula, but the Mediterranean scenery and mysterious storyline give it enough individuality to stand apart from more generic alternatives.

Rating: 6/10
